title: Lemon Trifle
subtitle: Sponge with lemon curd, a sharp lemon custard, and cream
excerpt: A bright, sharp trifle with lemon-soaked sponge, a lemon-zested custard, and whipped cream, no fruit layer, no sherry, just clean citrus flavour in every spoonful.
sourceNotes: A British spring-table variant of the classic trifle, substituting lemon curd and lemon custard for the traditional fruit and sherry layers. Lemon trifles appear in British home-cooking collections from the late 20th century as a fresher alternative to the richer Christmas version.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the sponge and custard layers the day before and keep in the fridge overnight. Add the cream layer up to 3 hours before serving.

content.text: Lemon trifle is a brighter, sharper take on the classic layered dessert, sponge fingers soaked in lemon juice, topped with a zesty lemon custard and softly whipped cream. There is no fruit layer and no alcohol; the whole flavour is built from lemon at every stage. The custard must be made with good fresh lemons: the zest steeped in the warm milk before the eggs are added gives it a clean, aromatic quality that juice alone cannot.

items.prepNote: from about 2 lemons, use this to soak the sponge

content.text: Mix the lemon juice with the tablespoon of caster sugar and 2 tablespoons of cold water until the sugar dissolves. Arrange the sponge fingers in a single layer across the base of a glass trifle dish and pour the lemon soaking liquid evenly over them. Leave for 5 minutes to absorb.

Add the lemon zest to the milk in a medium saucepan and heat gently to just below boiling. Remove from the heat and leave to infuse for 15 minutes, then strain the milk through a sieve to remove the zest. Return the infused milk to the saucepan. Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar, cornflour, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl until smooth. Reheat the lemon milk to steaming, then pour slowly into the egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return to the saucepan and stir continuously over a low-medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Pour through a sieve over the soaked sponge layer, press cling film to the surface, and leave to cool.

Once the custard is at room temperature, chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours. Whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks and spread over the custard. Arrange thin lemon slices on top, or scatter a little extra lemon zest to finish.

items.symptom: Custard tastes flat or not very lemony
items.cause: The zest was not left long enough to infuse, or the lemons were not freshly zested.
items.fix: Increase the infusion time to 20 minutes before straining. For a more pronounced flavour, add 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice to the finished custard off the heat.

items.cause: The eggs cooked unevenly, or the milk was too hot when added.
items.fix: Strain through a fine-mesh sieve while still warm. Any small lumps will be caught by the sieve and the custard underneath will be smooth.

items.cause: The soaking liquid was too little or the sponge did not absorb evenly.
items.fix: Use a tablespoon to spoon any liquid that pools back over drier sections. If needed, add 1 to 2 tablespoons more lemon juice mixed with water.

content.text: Keeps well in the fridge for up to 2 days, covered. The lemon flavour deepens slightly on day two. Do not freeze.
